arxiv-2110-02489.title: How the magnetic field behaves during the motion of a highly conducting fluid under its own gravity–A new theoretical, relativistic approach
arxiv-2110-02489.creator: Panagiotis Mavrogiannis, Christos G. Tsagas
arxiv-2110-02489.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Panagiotis Mavrogiannis, Christos G. Tsagas. Within the context of general relativity we study in a fully covariant way the so-called Euler-Maxwell system of equations. In particular, on decomposing the aforementioned system into its 1 temporal and 1 + 2 spatial components at the ideal magnetohydrodynamic limit, we bring it in a simplified form that favors physical insight to the problem of a self-gravitating, magnetized fluid.

arxiv-2203-14096.title: Fourier Coefficients of Hilbert Modular Forms at Cusps
arxiv-2203-14096.creator: Tim Davis
arxiv-2203-14096.description: A 2022 arXiv research paper by Tim Davis. The aim of this article is to study the fields generated by the Fourier coefficients of Hilbert newforms at arbitrary cusps. Precisely, given a cuspidal Hilbert newform f f and a matrix σ \sigma in (a suitable conjugate of) the Hilbert modular group, we give a cyclotomic extension of the field generated by the Fourier coefficients at infinity which contains all the Fourier coefficients of f | | k σ f||_{k}\sigma .

arxiv-2403-18700.title: Bridging hadronic and vacuum structure by heavy quarkonia
arxiv-2403-18700.creator: Nicholas Miesch, Edward Shuryak, Ismail Zahed
arxiv-2403-18700.description: A 2024 arXiv research paper by Nicholas Miesch, Edward Shuryak, Ismail Zahed. We discuss the central and, mostly, spin-dependent potentials in heavy quarkonia b ¯ ​ b , c ¯ ​ c \bar{b}b,\bar{c}c , with two goals in mind. The first is phenomenological: using the splitting between the 1S and 2S pairs, as well as the 1P and 2P quartet masses, we obtain very accurate values of all matrix elements of the spin-depepdent potentials.

arxiv-2406-06823.title: Locally Interdependent Multi-Agent MDP: Theoretical Framework for Decentralized Agents with Dynamic Dependencies
arxiv-2406-06823.creator: Alex DeWeese, Guannan Qu
arxiv-2406-06823.description: Abstract Many multi-agent systems in practice are decentralized and have dynamically varying dependencies. There has been a lack of attempts in the literature to analyze these systems theoretically. In this paper, we propose and theoretically analyze a decentralized model with dynamically varying dependencies called the Locally Interdependent Multi-Agent MDP.

arxiv-2406-15481.title: Code-Switching Red-Teaming: LLM Evaluation for Safety and Multilingual Understanding
arxiv-2406-15481.creator: Haneul YooKAISTDaejeon, South Korea haneul.yoo@kaist.ac.kr, Yongjin YangKAIST AISeoul, South Korea dyyjkd@kaist.ac.kr Hwaran LeeNAVER AI LabSeongnam, South Korea hwaran.lee@navercorp.com
arxiv-2406-15481.description: Abstract As large language models (LLMs) have advanced rapidly, concerns regarding their safety have become prominent. In this paper, we discover that code-switching in red-teaming queries can effectively elicit undesirable behaviors of LLMs, which are common practices in natural language.

arxiv-2409-20183.title: Local equivalence of stabilizer states: a graphical characterisation
arxiv-2409-20183.creator: Nathan Claudet, Simon Perdrix
arxiv-2409-20183.description: Abstract Stabilizer states form a ubiquitous family of quantum states that can be graphically represented through the graph state formalism. A fundamental property of graph states is that applying a local complementation – a well-known and extensively studied graph transformation – results in a graph that represents the same entanglement as the original.

arxiv-2504-15987.description: Abstract The proliferation of hate speech on social media poses a significant threat to online communities, requiring effective detection systems. arxiv-2507-16912.title: Predicting the Properties of the Fallback Rate from Tidal Disruption Events: Investigating the Maximum Gravity Model
arxiv-2507-16912.creator: Julia Fancher, Ananya Bandopadhyay, Eric R. Coughlin, C. J. Nixon
arxiv-2507-16912.description: Abstract A star destroyed by the tidal field of a supermassive black hole (SMBH) in a tidal disruption event (TDE) gives rise to a luminous flare. TDEs are being detected at an ever-increasing rate, motivating the need for accurate models of their lightcurves.

pmc-12756665.description: BackgroundPhysical activity (PA) is feasible, safe, beneficial, and recommended for pediatric patients with cancer. Nevertheless, PA levels remain low due to treatment-related effects (eg, fatigue, pain), isolation and immunosuppression, geographic and transportation barriers, and limited access to population-specific programming. Delivering PA by videoconference may address some of these barriers.

pmc-12775543.title: Performance improvement of a vortex pump based on volute shape modification
pmc-12775543.creator: Kun Lan, Yaguang Heng, Qifeng Jiang, Yunchuan Tu, Chuan Wang, Jie Ge
pmc-12775543.description: Vortex pumps are widely used in many engineering fields because of their small size and high lift head. However, the efficiency of this pump is quite low compared with that of other pumps. Therefore, the objective of the present study is to increase the efficiency of a vortex pump while increasing the head and reducing the power consumption.
